text: When the favourite was sent over to the race just as Holmes found him
why: Holmes says he 'found him in the hands of a faker, and took the liberty of running him just as he was sent over,' so the time point is stated in the story.
Holmes has just promised that 'you shall know everything' at the racecourse, so an account given at this point is what the story has set up.

text: Who is the faker in whose hands Holmes found the horse?
why: The story has already shown Holmes recovering the horse from Silas Brown, whom he calls 'an old horse-faker,' so the question is one the reader has reason to ask and its wording does not supply the answer.
